saves.question: Where are my saves?
saves.answer: Most PC games keep saves in your user folder, for example Documents\My Games or AppData\LocalLow\<company>\<game>. Some keep them inside the game's own folder. SavePrism does not scan your PC; it shows the usual folders.
saves.link: See the usual folder for each kind of game

original.question: Is my original save changed?
original.answer: Only if you choose Overwrite current file. The default is Save as a new file, so the original stays as it was. Before any file is replaced, SavePrism keeps a copy you can put back from Backups.

games.question: Which games work?
games.answer: Games made with Unity, Unreal Engine, RPG Maker, Ren'Py, Godot, GameMaker and more, plus save codes from browser games. The full list is in the README. If a file can be read, its values appear right away.

notOpen.question: My file does not open — what now?
notOpen.answer: Check that it is the save itself, not a shortcut or a screenshot. Some games lock their saves; SavePrism says what it found. Still stuck? Copy file report and tell us on GitHub with the game's name.

ai.question: How do I use it with an AI tool?
ai.answer: Press Ask AI on any list to copy its values, then paste them into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. AI apps that support MCP, such as Claude Desktop, can connect directly: Settings → AI connection.

undo.question: How do I undo a change?
undo.answer: Press Ctrl+Z to undo and Ctrl+Y to redo, or Undo all in the bottom bar. After saving, open Backups to go back to an earlier version.

engine.rpgmaker-classic: RPG Maker XP / VX / VX Ace / 2000 / 2003

hint.rpgmaker-mv: MV has a www folder, MZ has js and data folders. Saves end in .rpgsave or .rmmzsave.
hint.rpgmaker-classic: Game.exe next to Game.ini. Saves end in .rxdata, .rvdata or .rvdata2.
hint.wolf-rpg: Game.exe with Data/BasicData. Saves are .sav files in the Save folder.
hint.unity: UnityPlayer.dll and a <game>_Data folder next to the .exe.
hint.unreal: An Engine folder next to the game's folder. Saves end in .sav.
hint.gamemaker: A data.win file next to the .exe.
hint.renpy: renpy and game folders. Saves end in .save.
hint.godot: One .exe with a .pck file of the same name.
hint.twine: Runs in a browser. Use the game's Save to disk or export option.
hint.flash: A .swf file. Saves are local shared objects (.sol).
hint.witcher3: Saves end in .sav in Documents\The Witcher 3\gamesaves.
hint.terraria: Characters (.plr) and worlds (.wld) in Documents\My Games\Terraria.
hint.neverwinter-nights: Saves are .sav folders in Documents or in the game's folder.
hint.kotor: Saves are .sav folders inside the game's folder, one per slot.
hint.ags: agssave.000 to agssave.999 next to the game.
hint.nscripter: nscript.dat or a .nsa file. Saves are save*.dat in the game's folder.
hint.emuera: Emuera.exe. Saves are .sav files in the game's folder or its sav folder.
hint.alicesoft: System 3.x keeps .asd saves in the game's folder; System 4 often uses SaveData.
hint.construct: Construct 2/3 games save in the browser; a .c2save/.c3save file is plain JSON.
hint.artemis: Saves are in the save folder next to the .exe.
hint.ets2: Profiles are in Documents\Euro Truck Simulator 2\profiles.
hint.ats: Profiles are in Documents\American Truck Simulator\profiles.
hint.retroarch: Save states (.state) and battery saves (.srm) under %APPDATA%\RetroArch.

note.rpgmaker-mv: MV uses www/save; MZ uses save.
note.rpgmaker-classic: The save can be in the game's folder or in its Save folder.
note.wolf-rpg: Saves are in the Save folder inside the game's folder.
note.unity: PlayerPrefs live in the Windows registry: export them with regedit. Easy Save files are under %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\<company>\<game>\.
note.unreal: The project name is the game's folder name.
note.renpy: Saves can also be in game/saves inside the game's folder.
note.twine: Browser storage: use the game's Save to disk / export option.
note.witcher3: The Documents folder may be moved to OneDrive.
note.satisfactory: The folder under your Steam/Epic ID holds the .sav files.
note.terraria: Players holds the characters; Worlds holds the worlds. The Documents folder may be moved to OneDrive.
note.neverwinter-nights: Enhanced Edition keeps saves in Documents; the classic game uses saves inside its folder.
note.kotor: Saves are the .sav files in the game folder, one folder per slot.
note.emuera: Saves are in the game folder, or in its sav folder when the game uses one.
note.nscripter: save1.dat ... and global.sav (or gloval.sav) in the game folder.
note.ags: Save slots are agssave.000 to agssave.999 next to the game.
note.alicesoft: System 3.x keeps saves in the game folder; System 4 games often use SaveData.
note.artemis: Saves are in the save folder next to the game executable.
note.construct: Construct 2/3 saves are usually in the browser storage; a .c2save/.c3save file is plain JSON and opens by content.
note.elden-ring: The folder under your Steam ID holds ER0000.sl2.
note.dark-souls-3: The folder under your Steam ID holds DS30000.sl2.
note.ets2: Each profile has save/<slot>/game.sii; set g_save_format to 2 for plain text.
note.ats: Each profile has save/<slot>/game.sii; set g_save_format to 2 for plain text.
note.retroarch: states and saves are the usual folders; save states may be RZIP-compressed (Save State File Compression).

SP-APP-001.fix: Restart SavePrism. If it keeps happening, report the code on the issue tracker.

SP-APP-003.reason: this file is read-only, so it cannot be saved
SP-APP-003.fix: Open a copy of the file, or wait for support for this format.

SP-APP-004.reason: "{{value}}" is not valid for this field
SP-APP-004.reasonPlain: the value is not valid for this field
SP-APP-004.fix: Type a value that fits the field's type.

SP-APP-005.reason: {{value}} is outside the allowed range for this field
SP-APP-005.reasonPlain: the number is outside the allowed range for this field
SP-APP-005.fix: Type a number inside the range shown for the field.

SP-APP-006.reason: a file with that name is already there
SP-APP-006.fix: Pick another name or another folder.

SP-APP-007.fix: Open the container and pick one of its values.

SP-APP-008.reason: the JSON export needs a different name
SP-APP-008.fix: Choose a name ending in .json that is not the open save file.

SP-APP-009.reason: SavePrism could not use its own state

SP-APP-010.reason: the JSON text is not valid
SP-APP-010.fix: Fix the highlighted place and apply again.

SP-APP-011.reason: the JSON text changes more than values
SP-APP-011.fix: Change only values; leave field names, list items and placeholders as they are.

SP-APP-012.reason: the third-party notices could not be opened
SP-APP-012.fix: Read them in the SavePrism install folder.

SP-APP-013.reason: there is no backup "{{name}}" of this file
SP-APP-013.reasonPlain: that backup is no longer there

SP-APP-014.reason: that backup does not open as a save
SP-APP-014.fix: Nothing was written. Pick another backup.

SP-APP-015.reason: that is too many values for one change

SP-APP-016.fix: Paste the whole code the game gave you.

SP-APP-017.reason: this save has no code to copy
SP-APP-017.fix: Use Save as to keep the edited file.

SP-APP-018.reason: that folder does not hold the game's data
SP-APP-018.fix: Pick the game's data folder or its game folder.

SP-APP-019.reason: this save has no sections that take names from a data folder
SP-APP-019.fix: Open an RPG Maker save to use game names.

SP-APP-020.fix: Pick another name, or change the value that is there.

SP-APP-021.fix: Add values in a JSON, Easy Save 3, SugarCube or RPG Maker list.

SP-APP-022.fix: Set it to 0, empty or off instead.

SP-APP-023.reason: the file changed on disk after you opened it
SP-APP-023.fix: Open the file again, or use Save as to keep your edits.

SP-APP-024.reason: an AI tool sent a value SavePrism cannot use
SP-APP-024.fix: Check the tool's arguments and try again.

SP-APP-025.reason: the file to compare with is encrypted, so it cannot be read
SP-APP-025.fix: Compare with an unencrypted copy of the save instead.

SP-APP-026.reason: the folder could not be opened
SP-APP-026.fix: Open it by hand in File Explorer.

SP-APP-027.reason: a file report can only be made for a regular file
SP-APP-027.fix: Pick the save file itself, not a folder or a shortcut.

SP-DET-001.reason: SavePrism does not know this file yet
SP-DET-001.fix: Attach a sample file to an issue so support can be added.

SP-DET-002.reason: SavePrism could not work out this file
SP-DET-002.fix: Try again with a smaller or unencrypted copy.

SP-ES3-001.reason: this is not an Easy Save 3 file
SP-ES3-001.fix: Check that you picked the game's save file.

SP-ES3-002.reason: this Easy Save 3 file holds something SavePrism cannot write
SP-ES3-002.fix: Open it read-only, or report a sample on the issue tracker.

SP-ES3-003.reason: this encrypted Easy Save 3 file is damaged
SP-ES3-003.fix: Restore it from a backup or from the game and try again.

SP-ES3-004.reason: that password did not open the file
SP-ES3-004.fix: Check the password in the game's Easy Save settings and try again.

SP-ES3-005.reason: this file is encrypted and needs its password
SP-ES3-005.fix: Enter the password used by the game and open the file again.

SP-CORE-007.reason: the file expands to too much data
SP-CORE-007.fix: The file may be damaged; try another copy.

SP-CORE-008.reason: the file is nested too deeply
SP-CORE-008.fix: The file may be damaged; try another copy.

SP-CORE-009.reason: the file holds too many values
SP-CORE-009.fix: Try another copy of the file.

SP-CORE-010.reason: the file has too many layers
SP-CORE-010.fix: Try another copy of the file.

SP-CORE-011.reason: that value is no longer in the file
SP-CORE-011.fix: Pick the value again from the tree; the path may have changed.

SP-CORE-012.reason: the change could not be applied
SP-CORE-012.fix: Try again; if it keeps failing, report the code on the issue tracker.

SP-IO-001.reason: the backup could not be made
SP-IO-001.fix: Check free disk space and the backup folder's permissions. Nothing was written.

SP-IO-002.reason: the temporary file could not be written
SP-IO-002.fix: Close the game and other programs that use the file, then try again.

SP-IO-003.reason: the file could not be replaced
SP-IO-003.fix: Close the game and other programs that use the file, check that it is not read-only, then try again.

SP-IO-004.reason: the saved file did not check out, so the backup was restored

SP-IO-005.reason: the saved file did not check out and the backup could not be restored
SP-IO-005.fix: Restore the file from the backup folder by hand and report the code on the issue tracker.

SP-IO-006.reason: no backup folder could be found
SP-IO-006.fix: Check that your user profile folder is available, then try again.

SP-IO-007.reason: the file could not be read
SP-IO-007.fix: Check that the file exists and can be read, then try again.

SP-RENPY-001.reason: this Ren'Py save is not a file SavePrism can read
SP-RENPY-001.fix: Open the save the game wrote, not a copy from another game.

SP-RENPY-002.reason: this Ren'Py save holds something SavePrism cannot write
SP-RENPY-002.fix: Open it read-only, or report a sample on the issue tracker.

SP-RENPY-003.reason: this Ren'Py save could not be written
SP-RENPY-003.fix: Open it read-only and keep a copy of the file.

SP-RENPY-004.reason: the Ren'Py key file could not be read
SP-RENPY-004.fix: Check that security_keys.txt exists and has a signing-key line, then open the save again.
